complexity_scope.guarantee: Upper success >=1-delta per instance with all-path deterministic cap. Dimension claim accompanies the fixed-confidence lower bound only.
complexity_scope.oracle: Choose (i,x) in [n] times R^d; receive exact scalar component p-jet, one query per reply.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Any output point xhat in R^d; Euclidean gradient norm <=epsilon.
complexity_scope.regime: Positive parameters; fixed p; all n>=1.
complexity_scope.resource: Complete component p-jet calls, including snapshot, sampled endpoint pairs, rejected trials and full endpoint verification; unrestricted internal computation.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper: verified Taylor-residual epochs with modified trial cap. Lower dimension: unrestricted randomized measurable adaptive component-query algorithms, including unbounded queries and unqueried outputs.

evidence.statement_check: Checked both separate conclusions and the explicit absence of confidence-optimality.

content.intended_use: Refine the main fixed-order minimax statement without asserting confidence-optimality.

proofs.locator: Proposition A.5 p.15; Proposition D.5 p.22; Appendix E and Remark E.1 pp.23–24
map: Appendix A uses m=ceil(sqrt(n)), B=64m, M=4(p^2+2^(p+1))L_p m^(p-1), r^p=p!epsilon/(4M), d0=M r^(p+1)/(2(p+1)!) and H=floor(Delta/(m d0))+1.

Lemma A.2 gives conditional bad-trial probability <=1/64. For Z_r counting bad trials, with zero padding after termination, E[2^Z_r]<=(65/64)^r. For r>=2H, nontermination implies Z_r>=r/2, giving probability <=(65/(64 sqrt(2)))^r<=exp(-r/4).
Proposition A.5 sets R_delta=2H+ceil(4 log(1/delta)); per-trial cost <=2n+2Bm and H=O_p(1+K_p m^(-1/p)) yield the claimed all-path bound.

For the lower dimension, Proposition D.5 requires D>=max{2048+512 log(N+2),128 log(128(N+1)T)}. Appendix E chooses T=Theta_p(K_p n^(-1/(2p))) in the nontrivial large-n regime and d=TD. Hidden-index and small-n constructions cover remaining regimes after adjusting C_p.

assumptions: Upper bound: for every x,y, [n^(-1)sum_i ||D^p f_i(x)-D^p f_i(y)||_op^2]^(1/2)<=L_p||x-y||.
Exact component queries return value and all derivatives through order p; internal computation, including exact global model minimization, is unrestricted.
Lower-bound dimension refers to Theorem 3.2's individual-smoothness class, not a delta-dependent hardness statement. No lower-order derivative bound is imposed.
statement.conclusion: An epsilon-stationary output, ||grad F(xhat)||<=epsilon, is achievable using O_p(K_p n^(1-1/(2p))+n[1+log(1/delta)]) queries on every execution path. The lower bound in Theorem 3.2 can be witnessed with d<=C_p(1+K_p n^(-1/(2p))) log(2+n+K_p n^(1-1/(2p))). Constants depend only on p. No matching delta dependence is claimed.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For finite d, f_i in C^p(R^d), F=n^(-1)sum_i f_i and initial point 0. Tensor operator norm is sup over unit direction vectors of the absolute multilinear evaluation. Set K_p=Delta L_p^(1/p) epsilon^(-(p+1)/p) and S_p=n+K_p n^(1-1/(2p)).
statement.parameter_domains: Fixed p>=2; n positive integer; arbitrary finite dimension for the upper bound; Delta,L_p,epsilon>0; 0<delta<1.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed integer p>=2, n>=1, positive Delta,L_p,epsilon and delta in (0,1), an algorithm succeeds for every admissible finite-dimensional instance with probability at least 1-delta over its private samples and obeys the stated cap on every path. For each randomized algorithm below a sufficiently small p-dependent multiple of S_p, a fixed hard instance for the constant-confidence lower bound exists within the stated dimension bound.
